svg.title: K11: a rolling update protects visitors from a bad release
svg.desc: Release v2 crashes at start. With maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1, Kubernetes starts one v2 Pod, which never becomes Ready, and refuses to remove any Ready v1 Pod. The three v1 Pods keep serving, the visitors are fine, and only the rollout is stuck. kubectl rollout undo returns to v1.

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The Friday release that Kubernetes saved

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Rolling updates keep the old version serving until the new one is Ready

svg.text: maxUnavailable: 0 · never remove a Ready v1 Pod until a v2 Pod is Ready

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The users are fine. Only the release is stuck.

svg.text: rollout status keeps waiting: 1 out of 3 new replicas updated. One v2 Pod in CrashLoopBackOff. The visitor still gets answers.

svg.text: kubectl rollout undo deployment/showdown puts v1 back. The cause was v2's PORT set to the word "eighty".
